title: How the Berne festival began in a hotel room
summary: The Swiss band invites him for a tour and then a small festival; he phones Cliff Leeman and Ralph Sutton to bring the rest of the Condon band, all expenses paid.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes, which I've been doing all my life - that kind of stuff - but they didn't know that. So, they were very impressed and I made very good friends with all these guys. Marvelous band. So, they invited me to Switzerland and I went and did a tour with them before they had--- I did just a small tour and then they said - we're going to have a jazz festival this year - we're going to try one; would you be interested in it? And, I said, well, certainly - you know - because it was a very good

band. So, I went back and after this little thing they set up - they set up a four day thing where that band played in many of the places in Berne, Switzerland and, then, a few days out in the mountain country. We played Ski Lodges and all kinds of things like that and, uh, it was such a success that they said - do you think that you could get the remaining members of the Condon Band over here-- and this is how this all started. This was in our hotel room.
And, this is what you're going to be doing this coming Spring---
Yes, but I've done it now - this will be the fourth year.
Yeah but I mean--- all right - okay.

Yeah. So, I said well, there's one way we can find out; if you can afford these phone calls, I'll find out right now for you. So, we phoned -- I got hold of Cliff Leeman and I got hold of the piano player, you know, Ralph Sutton and we lined the whole thing up and all very agreeable; First, before I made the phone call, I said - what can you afford to pay these guys to come over; he said - well, you tell them, this amount of money plus transportation, plus their hotel and food.
